entities.name: L5 nerve root
observations: Courses over the anterior sacral ala and is at risk from anterior iliosacral screw penetration.
Injury is associated with foot drop; great toe dorsiflexion is an L5-predominant motor test.

entities.name: Iliosacral screw placement
observations: Anterior penetration through the sacral ala can compress or injure the L5 nerve root.

entities.name: Great toe dorsiflexion
observations: Great toe dorsiflexion, primarily via extensor hallucis longus, is a classic L5-predominant motor function and is expected to weaken with L5-root injury.

entities.name: Anterior screw L5 injury
observations: Anterior iliosacral screw penetration through the sacral ala most threatens L5 and may cause foot drop; among the choices, great toe dorsiflexion is the best motor deficit.
